## 2. Instructions {.unnumbered}

This assessment is intended to evaluate your suitability for the Software Development Internship at NTS.

## 3. About Your Assessor {.unnumbered}

Your assessor will be **Daniel Mkony** throughout this assessment. His role is to guide you, answer your questions, review your progress, and help you overcome technical challenges.

**Microsoft Teams contact:** Daniel Mkony. Use Microsoft Teams to contact your assessor when you need clarification or technical support during the assessment.

## 5. How to Complete the Assessment {.unnumbered}

### Use This Book as the Answer Sheet

The candidate must edit this Quarto Book directly.

For every task:

1. Read the objective and instructions carefully.
2. Complete the requested practical work.
3. Write your answer directly in the relevant `.qmd` file.
4. Add screenshots, source code, diagrams, tables, or other evidence where requested.
5. Save the file.
6. Review the updated page in the browser.
7. Correct any formatting or content problems before moving to the next task.

Do not delete the original questions or headings unless instructed to do so.

Example:

```markdown

## Task 2.1 — Previous Projects {.unnumbered}

### Answer {.unnumbered}

I developed an IoT medicine cabinet using ESP32 and Firebase.

### Technologies Used {.unnumbered}

- ESP32
- Firebase
- Arduino IDE

### Challenges {.unnumbered}

The main challenge was unstable Wi-Fi connectivity.

### Solution {.unnumbered}

I added automatic reconnection logic.
```

### Project 1: StallSeeker (Real-Time Android Food Stall Discovery Application) {.unnumbered}

#### My Responsibilities {.unnumbered}
- Developed the Android application frontend using Flutter and Dart for nearby food stall discovery, search, filters, and self-collect bookings.
- Implemented customer and vendor features using Firebase Authentication, Firestore, and Storage for account access, menus, and stock management.
- Integrated Google Maps and GPS for live vendor tracking/navigation and Stripe sandbox payments.
- Created automated Android UI testing scripts using Appium, Python, and pytest with HTML reporting.

#### Technologies Used {.unnumbered}
- Flutter & Dart
- Firebase (Authentication, Cloud Firestore, Firebase Storage, Cloud Messaging, Cloud Functions)
- Google Maps API & GPS
- Stripe Sandbox API
- Appium, Python, pytest

#### Challenges Experienced {.unnumbered}
- Making the UI fit well on different screen sizes like web browsers, tablets, and phones without layout issues.
- Fixing a navigation bug where going back to a previous page refreshed the whole screen and cleared the user's progress.

#### Solutions {.unnumbered}
- Adjusted the layout sizes and tested the app manually on different screen sizes and emulators.
- Updated the page navigation and saved the page state so going back keeps the user's data without reloading everything.

## 9. Previewing the Book {.unnumbered}

The Quarto preview is already running from the project directory.

The current preview address is:

```text
http://localhost:[port]/
```

The command used to start the preview is:

```powershell
quarto preview
```

The PowerShell terminal shows:

```text
Watching files for changes
```

This means Quarto is monitoring the project files.

When you edit and save a `.qmd` file, Quarto should rebuild the changed page and refresh the browser automatically.

## 10. Refreshing the Browser {.unnumbered}

After editing a chapter:

1. Save the file using `Ctrl + S`.
2. Return to the browser.
3. Wait briefly for Quarto to rebuild the page.
4. Check that your new answer appears correctly.

When the page does not refresh automatically, use:

```text
Ctrl + R
```

For a full browser refresh, use:

```text
Ctrl + Shift + R
```

## 11. Restarting the Quarto Preview {.unnumbered}

To stop the currently running preview, click inside the PowerShell terminal and press:

```text
Ctrl + C
```

To return to the project folder, run:

```powershell
cd C:\internship\software-development-internship
```

To start the preview again, run:

```powershell
quarto preview
```

After the preview starts, open the address shown in the terminal, normally:

```text
http://localhost:[port]/ 
```

The port number may be different after restarting. Always use the address displayed by Quarto in the terminal.

## 12. Rendering the Final Book {.unnumbered}

Before final submission, stop the preview using:

```text
Ctrl + C
```

Then generate the complete final book with:

```powershell
quarto render
```

This command builds all chapters and checks whether the project can be rendered successfully.

If the render is successful, Quarto will place the generated website in the output folder configured in `_quarto.yml`.

The output folder is normally one of the following:

```text
_site
```

or:

```text
_book
```

Open the generated folder and confirm that all expected HTML pages are present.

## 13. Final Review Checklist {.unnumbered}

Before publishing or submitting the assessment, confirm that:

- [ ] Every required question has been answered.
- [ ] All chapter files have been saved.
- [ ] No placeholder text remains.
- [ ] Images and screenshots display correctly.
- [ ] Code blocks are readable and correctly formatted.
- [ ] Links work.
- [ ] Tables display correctly.
- [ ] Required evidence has been added.
- [ ] Personal or confidential information has not been included unnecessarily.
- [ ] `quarto render` completes without errors.
- [ ] The final website has been reviewed in the browser.

## 14. Publishing the Book {.unnumbered}

After completing and reviewing the assessment, start the Quarto publishing process with:

```powershell
quarto publish
```

Quarto will ask you to select or configure a publishing destination.

When the project has already been configured for GitHub Pages, the publishing command may be:

```powershell
quarto publish gh-pages
```

Only publish the book after:

1. completing all chapters;
2. running `quarto render`;
3. fixing all rendering errors;
4. reviewing the final generated pages;
5. receiving confirmation from the supervisor that publishing is required.

## 15. Important Notes {.unnumbered}

- Keep the PowerShell preview terminal open while editing.
- Do not run several `quarto preview` commands at the same time.
- Always save your file before checking the browser.
- Do not edit files inside `_site` or `_book` because those folders contain generated output.
- Edit only the source `.qmd`, YAML, image, and supporting project files.
- If the terminal reports an error, read the filename and line number shown, correct the source file, save it, and run the command again.
